alignments.note: Construct noun keeps only its own word. The accepted alignment additionally gave it *have* as a recast construct relation, but MACULA tags s002 רֵיחַ `Ncmsa` (absolute) and s003 `Ncmpc`, so no construct relation between fragrance and oils stands in the projection and s003 is the regens rather than the rectum; rule 43 places the *have* elsewhere.

The ASV recasts the clause possessively (*Thine oils have a goodly fragrance*). No הָיָה stands here, no written verb is rendered by *have*, and the suffix already holds *Thine*, so under rule 43's counting rider it is not a home for a second word; the לְ is the clause's one relational morpheme on which the ASV has spent nothing, and the *have* is what it is rendered by, exactly as `שָׁפְרָה עָלָי` → *I have a goodly heritage* gives *goodly* to the adjective and *have* to the preposition. Two materially available alternatives: *have* `added` under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause, and *have* folded into שְׁמָנֶי as a recast construct relation (the accepted reading). The `added` branch is rejected because rule 43 reaches it only where no preposition or suffix is left with an English word to take, and this preposition is.
Substantive with its supplied indefinite article (rule 15), discontinuous around the adjective (rule 25).
Predicate adjective recast attributively as *goodly*; rule 43 is explicit that a word so rendered is not a copula and does not carry the *have*.
Construct noun keeps its own word.
The italic comparative *as* answers to no morpheme: the Hebrew predicate is a bare nominal (rules 7, 30).
Fronted nominal predicate with the construction-supplied copula (rule 20); שְׁמֶךָ is the subject and takes only its own English.
Verb with its phrasal particle; the head stays on the lexical verb (rule 44).
עַל־כֵּן fused into one English word (rule 30), headed on the governing first morpheme (rule 23).
Finite verb with the fronted auxiliary *do* the inverted English clause requires; no interrogative morpheme stands here, so the auxiliary is the verb's own (rule 17).
No article morpheme is present, so the supplied *the* joins the noun (rule 15).
Object suffix takes the object pronoun (rule 18).

review_notes: Fourteen source and nineteen target IDs each partitioned once in the corrected array.

The single change is t003 *have*: moved from s003 שְׁמָנֶי to s001 לְ. The accepted note's premise — that s003 is the nomen rectum carrying a construct relation the ASV recast — is contradicted by the token table, which tags s002 רֵיחַ absolute (`Ncmsa`) and s003 construct (`Ncmpc`).

Rule 43's enumeration of what can carry a *have* does not include a noun, and its `added` branch is reached only where no preposition or suffix is left unspent; here the לְ is unspent, so the word is placed on it rather than marked `added`. Both alternatives are named in that unit's note under rule 8.
The rest of the verse is unchanged, including the `added` italic *as* and the עַל־כֵּן fusion.
